translations.answer: DeepMimic combines a phase-conditioned state, imitation and task rewards, Reference State Initialization (RSI), and Early Termination (ET) to learn several simulated skills. These mechanisms show that examples can shape policy search effectively; they do not prove that the same motion can be deployed directly on a physical humanoid.
translations.applicability.assumptions.0: The reference motion has been matched to the character morphology and has a reliable phase definition.
translations.applicability.assumptions.1: Dynamics, contact, and actuator boundaries are validated separately for the deployment platform.
translations.applicability.controllers.0: PPO policy combining imitation and task objectives with PD targets.
translations.applicability.environments.0: Physics-based character simulations reported in the paper.
translations.applicability.robots.0: Simulated bipedal characters; not evidence from a physical humanoid.
translations.confidence_rationale: Multi-skill simulations and ablations support RSI, ET, and combined imitation/task rewards. Experiments use simulated characters and generally one training run, so they cannot establish hardware reliability.
translations.evidence.0.locator: Figures 2–7, Table 4, Sections 3–6, and the appendix.
translations.evidence.0.note: Defines phase state, imitation/task rewards, RSI/ET, PPO, and the skill ablations.
translations.evidence.0.title: DeepMimic: Example-Guided Deep Reinforcement Learning of Physics-Based Character Skills
translations.title: Why does DeepMimic learn skills from examples, and does that establish hardware readiness?
